## Semantic checks
The Context uses a finite DAG, genuinely disjoint covered chains, the actual supplied forward supershortcut witnesses, and original-graph first-entry selectors. The normalized graph is the actual augmented graph filtered by the fixed original source. Distance minimizes the actual finite set of chain labels on a valid route for originally reachable pairs; it is zero by convention otherwise. Important pairs and raw potential are the actual original-source/first-entry demand image and finite sum, not arbitrary progress oracles.

ChainInternalRedundancy constructs a real preprocessing route between originally reachable covered vertices of the same chain. Acyclicity makes their chain order forward, and the chain's actual witness supplies its edges. All support vertices have the single common label, so the route passes every source filter. Its literal recursive substitution removes every inserted dart occurrence from any allowed walk, retaining the old augmented edges and never adding a chain label. This proves equality of each normalized distance and then the entire raw potential, even for arbitrary H. The arbitrary-H claim concerns this defined normalized distance, including its original-unreachable zero convention; it does not assert that arbitrary illegal H preserves ordinary graph reachability. The source comments correctly say normalized distance.

ChainPositiveChoices starts from a strictly smaller actual raw potential. Finite-sum comparison supplies an actually improved important demand. An attained minimizing new route cannot already be allowed in the old state; an explicitly located offending dart must therefore be exactly the inserted edge, not a base or old shortcut. Legality of H and the inserted candidate is used critically to transport its prefix reachability back to the original graph. At a covered destination with different endpoint labels, the unchanged-source filter forces that destination to be the original source's first chain entry. Actual first-entry inheritance then makes the inserted pair itself important. No rebased shortest-subpath optimality or quantitative progress inequality is used.

The previously checked global saturated-edge redundancy, on the same original selectors, makes an important strict-saving edge unsaturated. The new internal-route theorem removes the same-covered-label case. The final complete dichotomy explicitly retains uncovered destinations and otherwise concludes membership in the actual current unsaturated important set. It does not silently discard legal uncovered-head candidates or assert they are unprofitable. Empty improvement domains are handled by contradiction from strict drop, without assumed witnesses. Endpoint label multiplicity is finite-set cardinality, as required by the substituted routes.

These lemmas classify actual positive legal choices and discharge same-covered-chain redundancy. They do not complete the higher-layer phase/progress bound, eliminate uncovered-head cases, or prove the paper's unresolved sharper shortcut-size theorem.
